abstract: The transition of the media industry to Internet Protocol (IP)-based networking protocols and workflows is well underway. Millions of users streaming audio and video daily believe that the transition and the hard work evolving to IP-based network transports is done and behind us, while the reality is that the revolution is far from over. Ongoing is the retooling of the entire content workflow of creation, editing, post-production, archiving, and delivery of professional media to leverage IP-based networks and protocols. This ongoing retooling handles networking situations and user demands that go well above the now seemingly mundane (but still surprisingly complex) task of reliably delivering prerecorded video on demand (VOD) content over well-behaved, reliable broadband that was seen as the “big” streaming challenge to achieve just a few years ago.

authors.bio: Glenn Deen is a Comcast distinguished engineer and the technical advisor to the IETF MOPS Media Operations Group. He is the chair of the IETF Trust and co-chairs the IETF Adaptive DNS Discovery (ADD) Group. He co-chairs the Streaming Video Alliance Network & Transport Group and is the treasurer of the Streaming Video Alliance.
authors.name: Glenn Deen

authors.bio: Leslie Daigle is currently the principal at Thinking Cat Enterprises. She has been working at the intersection of technology, business/economics, and policy to drive effective change for more than 20 years. She is the co-chair of the Media Operations (MOPS) Working Group and the co-host of the TechSequences podcast.
authors.name: Leslie Daigle

authors.bio: Kyle Rose, a 19-year veteran of Cambridge, MA-based Akamai Technologies, is a system architect focused on security, release architecture, and network performance. He is also an active participant of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).
authors.name: Kyle Rose
